title: Bag-Life Length Measured from Dispensed Fills, Tailwise Pharmacy Renewals
content:
*Pharmacy dispensing analytics note.*

On a renewal Tailwise Pharmacy places by itself, the days' supply per fill is the bag-life length: how many days one fill of the renewed prescription actually lasted, read from its dispensed fills on the pharmacy ledger.

**Measured interval.** The calendar days from the renewed prescription's first dispensed fill to its most recent dispensed fill, divided by its dispensed fills less one, rounded down to a whole day.

## Rule

| Dispensed fills of the renewed prescription | Any of them dispensed under an early-refill override (travel or lost or damaged)? | Bag-life length |
|---|---|---|
| 4 or more | none | the measured interval |
| at least 2 but fewer than 4 | none | the measured interval plus the written days' supply per fill, halved and rounded down to a whole day |
| 2 or more | at least one | the written days' supply per fill |
| fewer than 2 | | the written days' supply per fill |

## Worked cases (hypothetical; prescription written for 30 days)

- Fills on 2026-01-10, 2026-02-14, 2026-03-21 and 2026-04-25, none under an override: 105 calendar days divided by 3 is 35 days.
- Fills on 2026-01-10, 2026-02-14 and 2026-03-21, none under an override: measured interval 70 divided by 2, 35 days; 35 plus 30 is 65, halved is 32.5, rounded down: 32 days.
- Five fills, one of them a travel override: 30 days, the written days' supply.

The override reason is the one recorded on each dispensed fill, over the whole life of the prescription.
